authority.alpha_prerequisite: Keep RRFlow reasoning and discovery adaptive while making durable effects, evidence, ownership, and navigation trustworthy; remove the execution-map shadow authority and make linked records mechanically discoverable.

current_behavior: docs/roadmap/rrflow-1.0-execution-map.md is 4,117 lines and combines authoring procedure, architecture restatement, current implementation audit, future gate instructions, 96 completed journal/receipt blocks, run commands, and stop conditions. It shadows the roadmap and POA&M, forces AGENTS.md to append every future journal into the same growing file, and depends on manually synchronized Markdown indexes. Related architecture text also treats a fully committed project snapshot and closed routine graph as prerequisites to exploration, while six SDK records repeat projections of one executable protocol catalogue.
target_behavior: Turn the execution-map coordinate into a stable links-only portal. Author the change routine, implementation navigation, and generated-surface design as small linked records. Move all 96 legacy journal blocks without byte changes into individually coordinated evidence records grouped by gate, and record this package the same way. Change the literal AGENTS.md rule so one linked journal record plus regenerated indexes satisfies it. Add a generic marker-driven navigation maintainer that discovers record metadata and derives index entries, use it for the execution, journal, roadmap-chapter, POA&M-record, and SDK portals, and enforce freshness in documentation policy. Establish adaptive reasoning with governed effects: exploration and semantic planning remain flexible; closed validation is required at authorization, persistence, external-effect, replay, and evidence boundaries. State that the executable operation/capability catalogue is the single source from which internal dispatch, OpenAPI, SDK bindings/models, reference projections, and conformance matrices are generated.
unchanged_behavior: README.md remains the bootstrap identity/current-status owner; the objective owns measurable outcomes; the roadmap parent and gate chapters own dependency order and completion evidence; the POA&M parent owns deficiency lifecycle status.

All roadmap checkboxes, gate counts, POA&M priorities/statuses, the active D-01 executable item, product version 1.0.0, implementation behavior, build outputs, remotes, and release/promotion state remain unchanged.
Every legacy journal text block remains byte-for-byte intact and addressable; extraction changes location and metadata only, not its historical claim, command result, limitation, or revision.

RrdEngine remains the sole authority for authenticated durable mutation and accepted external-effect receipts. Generated indexes, schemas, clients, docs, traces, and adapters remain projections and cannot become lifecycle or semantic authorities.

The existing active-change validator remains the current repository effect-boundary check in this package; the new doctrine clarifies that it does not schema, capture, or constrain private analysis and exploratory reasoning.
